title: Number of Divisible Triplet Sums
summary: For an integer array nums and a divisor d, count the triplets (i, j, k) where i < j < k and the sum of nums[i], nums[j], and nums[k] is divisible by d.
statement: For an integer array nums and a divisor d, count the triplets (i, j, k) where i < j < k and the sum of nums[i], nums[j], and nums[k] is divisible by d.
constraints: nums contains positive integers and d is positive.
Count index triples i<j<k whose three values sum to a multiple of d.
Different index choices count separately even when values repeat.
hints: For fixed middle and right indices, an earlier value must have one specific remainder.
Count remainders of indices before middle and query the needed complement for every later right index.
Add counts[(-nums[j]-nums[k]) mod d], then insert nums[j] only after processing its right partners.
Delayed insertion enforces i<j, the inner scan enforces j<k, and the remainder complement is equivalent to divisibility.
editorial: Delayed insertion enforces i<j, the inner scan enforces j<k, and the remainder complement is equivalent to divisibility.

tests.explanation: Index triples (0,1,2), (0,2,4), and (1,2,4) have sums divisible by five.
Every choice of three among four indices sums to nine, producing four triplets.
